title: Multitask graph-policy attitude control
description: One compact learned policy supports smooth attitude tracking and aggressive flight recovery.
introduction: Normal flight rewards smooth, accurate tracking; recovery from a disturbed or falling state calls for rapid stabilization. This project trains one compact graph policy to balance those objectives and run directly on a flight controller.

problem.heading: Tracking and recovery demand different behaviour.
paragraphs: A controller tuned mainly for smooth commands can respond too slowly to an extreme initial state. A controller that always prioritizes rapid correction can become unnecessarily aggressive during ordinary attitude tracking.
An onboard method must express that trade-off while fitting the computation available on a small aerial vehicle. The research explores a shared policy conditioned by task priorities.

approach.heading: Encode state, priorities and actions in a graph policy.
paragraphs: The graph policy represents relationships between the vehicle state, task weights and attitude-control commands. Task weights specify the relative priorities of tracking, stabilization and smoothness within the same network.

The policy is trained with multitask soft actor–critic in parallel Isaac Gym simulations. The published implementation has 697 learned parameters and operates onboard a Pixhawk 6X at approximately 400 Hz, without a companion computer.
The same policy is used for normal attitude tracking and aggressive recovery. The training visualization and physical flight recordings are presented as different forms of evidence.

evidence.label: Onboard deployment
evidence.text: The published implementation reports a 697-parameter policy running at approximately 400 Hz on a Pixhawk 6X. Both normal tracking and aggressive recovery use the same onboard policy.

evidence.label: Published recovery campaign
evidence.text: The published campaign reports 13 successful recoveries in 13 tests, with complete rotor disengagement for 1–3 seconds before recovery. These are the conditions of that test campaign, rather than a general reliability guarantee.

evidence.label: Training environment
evidence.text: The Isaac Gym recording visualizes simulated training. It is separate from the outdoor recovery and attitude-tracking demonstrations.
